turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi there, how are you feeling today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My grandson keeps telling me to do online banking. Is it safe?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's generally very safe if you use your bank's official app or website and keep your password private.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Different question. I'm finally ditching my car for commuting, and I need to pick a new routine.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me lay out all the options first. Don't interrupt.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could cycle to the park and ride, then take the express bus the rest of the way.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Another way is the train from my village, which only runs twice an hour.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or I join my neighbour's car share to the tram terminus and ride the tram in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's it. Now you can comment.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If you want the most flexibility, cycling plus the express bus means you're never waiting on anyone. The train works too if you're the kind of person who's always early.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I worry about those scam messages.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a smart worry. Your bank will never ask for your full password or ask you to move money by text or phone call.
